root_cause.text: `pn_socket_autobind()` incorrectly assumes that an `-EINVAL` return value from `pn_socket_bind()` always indicates the socket was already bound, triggering a kernel panic via `BUG_ON()` when the error is actually caused by an invalid socket state (`sk_state != TCP_CLOSE`) on an unbound socket.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description and diff show that `pn_socket_bind()` returns `-EINVAL` when `sk->sk_state` is not `TCP_CLOSE` even if the socket is unbound (where `pn_port()` is still 0), which triggers the `BUG_ON(!pn_port(pn_sk(sock->sk)->sobject))` assertion. The patch resolves this by propagating the `-EINVAL` error instead of calling `BUG_ON()` when the port is zero.

candidates.rationale: This check incorrectly assumes that any error other than -EINVAL should be propagated, while -EINVAL itself is assumed to only mean the socket was already bound. However, -EINVAL can also be returned if the socket state is invalid.
This BUG_ON triggers a kernel panic when pn_socket_bind() returns -EINVAL on an unbound socket (due to an invalid socket state), because the port of an unbound socket is 0.

vuln_statements.explanation: This check incorrectly assumes that any error other than -EINVAL should be propagated, while -EINVAL itself is assumed to only mean the socket was already bound.
